precepts.text: Balaam also the son of Beor, the soothsayer, did the children of Israel slay with the sword. God got tired of him and had him put to death.
precepts.point: When he looked on Amalek: that is what you call the Israelis today. Amalek was the first of the nations that fought against us, but his latter end shall be that he perish for ever. The Kenites shall be wasted until Asshur, the Assyrians, carry them away captive; Judges 1:16 tells you about the Kenites. Ships shall come from the coast of Chittim, and shall afflict Asshur, and shall afflict Eber: write down 1 Maccabees 1:1 and 8:5.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

precepts.why:
Balaam dealt with enchantments, which lets us know he was a witch, a soothsayer, a diviner. When it says “the spirit of God came upon him”, notice the little s: this is on the left hand side. It is not the Holy Spirit coming on Balaam. He would fall into trances with his eyes wide open and see visions, and he knew it was the Lord sending that spirit upon him, which is why he told Balak he could not go beyond the commandment of the Lord. Even so, he saw Christ only from afar: “I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not nigh”, because he is not an Israelite.

What happened to Balaam? “Balaam also the son of Beor, the soothsayer, did the children of Israel slay with the sword among them that were slain by them.” What was he? The soothsayer: a witch, a warlock.

The Lord had used that witch, sending unrighteous angels to tell him this and tell him that. Then he told the Israelites: kill Balaam, destroy him; he is not our people. God got tired of him and had him put to death.

That is the end of the false prophet. Balaam could see all the way to the latter days and speak blessings over Israel, but his gift came from the left hand side, and he was slain among the enemies of Israel.

precepts.text: The inheritance of the half tribe of Manasseh, all Bashan.
precepts.point: Carmel was Judah's and Bashan was Manasseh's.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
Jeremiah 50:19 says Israel “shall feed on Carmel and Bashan”. Carmel was Judah's; now Bashan. Joshua 13 shows it: “And Moses gave inheritance unto the half tribe of Manasseh: and this was the possession of the half tribe of the children of Manasseh by their families.” “And their coast was from Mahanaim, all Bashan, all the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all the towns of Jair”. Bashan belonged to Manasseh.

Read Jeremiah 50:19 again so you get the thought: “And I will bring Israel again to his habitation, and he shall feed on Carmel and Bashan, and his soul shall be satisfied upon mount Ephraim and Gilead.” God is bringing Israel back to the very lands the tribes were given at the beginning.

Now see how it gets switched around in Obadiah. “And they of the south shall possess the mount of Esau; and they of the plain the Philistines: and they shall possess the fields of Ephraim, and the fields of Samaria: and Benjamin shall possess Gilead.” Benjamin shall possess Gilead. The tribes come back to the land, but the land is shared out anew.

Verse 20 goes on: “the captivity of this host of the children of Israel shall possess that of the Canaanites, even unto Zarephath”. The land of the Canaanites is the land of Israel, and Zarephath is Lebanon. “and the captivity of Jerusalem, which is in Sepharad, shall possess the cities of the south.” Sepharad is the Asia Minor region and Spain. Our people scattered there come home and take the cities of the south.

precepts.text: Balaam the son of Beor, the soothsayer, did the children of Israel slay with the sword among them that were slain by them.
precepts.point: Balaam also the son of Beor they slew with the sword. Balaam was a soothsayer, a diviner; he was a witch, so to speak.

note.label: Numbers 31: Vengeance on the Midianites

precepts.why:
They slew all the males and the five kings of Midian, Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur and Reba, and “Balaam also the son of Beor they slew with the sword.” Joshua tells who Balaam was: “Balaam also the son of Beor, the soothsayer, did the children of Israel slay with the sword among them that were slain by them.”

Balaam was a soothsayer, a diviner; he was a witch, so to speak. That is the man Israel slew with the sword among the Midianites.

precepts.text: I will not drive them out before thee in one year, but by little and little, until thou be increased and inherit the land.
precepts.point: The nations were also left among Israel to prove them, whether they would keep the commandments of the Most High, and so that the generations which had not known the wars of Canaan might be taught war. We all know what ended up happening with that proving, and it comes later on as we read.

note.label: Joshua 13: Much Land Yet to Be Possessed

precepts.why:
Joshua is old and stricken in years, “and there remaineth yet very much land to be possessed.” The Most High had already said how it would go: “I will not drive them out from before thee in one year; lest the land become desolate, and the beast of the field multiply against thee. By little and little I will drive them out from before thee, until thou be increased, and inherit the land.”

He was not going to drive out these nations in one year, but little and little as Israel increased, so much land still remained when Joshua was old.

precepts.text: These are the nations the Most High left to prove Israel, that the generations might know, to teach them war.
precepts.point: The nations were also left among Israel to prove them, whether they would keep the commandments of the Most High, and so that the generations which had not known the wars of Canaan might be taught war. We all know what ended up happening with that proving, and it comes later on as we read.

note.label: Joshua 13: Much Land Yet to Be Possessed

precepts.why:
The nations were also left among Israel for a reason: “Now these are the nations which the Lord left, to prove Israel by them, even as many of Israel as had not known all the wars of Canaan; Only that the generations of the children of Israel might know, to teach them war, at the least such as before knew nothing thereof”.

The Most High left them to prove Israel, whether they would keep the commandments of the Most High, and so that the generations which had not known the wars of Canaan might be taught war. That is why very much land remained to be possessed. We all know what ended up happening with that proving, and it comes later on as we read.

precepts.text: Ye shall divide the land by lot for an inheritance among your families; the command was given long before.
precepts.point: The land is to be divided only unto the Israelites: unto the nine tribes and the half tribe of Manasseh, for the other two and a half tribes had already received theirs. It had already been told that these lands must be divided among our people.

note.label: Joshua 13: Much Land Yet to Be Possessed

precepts.why:
Long before Joshua ever stood over this land, the command was already given: “And ye shall divide the land by lot for an inheritance among your families: and to the more ye shall give the more inheritance, and to the fewer ye shall give the less inheritance: every man’s inheritance shall be in the place where his lot falleth; according to the tribes of your fathers ye shall inherit.”

That is why the Most High tells Joshua, “only divide thou it by lot unto the Israelites for an inheritance, as I have commanded thee.” The driving out of the inhabitants of the hill country of Lebanon and all the Sidonians is the Most High's own work; Joshua's part is only to divide it by lot, the way it was commanded back in Numbers. It had already been told that these lands must be divided among our people, and among no one else.

precepts.text: Joshua gave the land for an inheritance unto Israel according to their divisions by their tribes.
precepts.point: The land is to be divided only unto the Israelites: unto the nine tribes and the half tribe of Manasseh, for the other two and a half tribes had already received theirs. It had already been told that these lands must be divided among our people.

note.label: Joshua 13: Much Land Yet to Be Possessed

precepts.why:
“So Joshua took the whole land, according to all that the Lord said unto Moses; and Joshua gave it for an inheritance unto Israel according to their divisions by their tribes. And the land rested from war.” What was commanded to Moses in Numbers, Joshua carried out: the land given for an inheritance unto Israel, tribe by tribe.

So when the Most High says “divide this land for an inheritance unto the nine tribes, and the half tribe of Manasseh”, it is only the Israelites who receive it. The other two and a half tribes had already received theirs, and now the rest of the land is divided among the rest of our people, according to their divisions by their tribes.

precepts.text: Thou shalt have no inheritance in their land; I am thy part and thine inheritance among the children of Israel.
precepts.point: Only unto the tribe of Levi he gave none inheritance; the sacrifices of the Lord God of Israel made by fire are their inheritance. The Most High had already said the same thing way back to Aaron, that Levi would have no inheritance in the land but would live among the people, and what was stated back then is being carried out in what we are reading now.

note.label: Joshua 13: Much Land Yet to Be Possessed

precepts.why:
“Only unto the tribe of Levi he gave none inheritance; the sacrifices of the Lord God of Israel made by fire are their inheritance, as he said unto them.” Where did he say it? Way back to Aaron: “Thou shalt have no inheritance in their land, neither shalt thou have any part among them: I am thy part and thine inheritance among the children of Israel.”

Levi would have no inheritance in the land; he would live among the people, and the Lord himself would be his part. What was stated back then to Aaron is being carried out in what we are reading now: while the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half tribe of Manasseh hold the inheritance Moses gave them beyond Jordan eastward, Levi's inheritance is the sacrifices of the Lord made by fire, exactly as he said.

precepts.text: The same Balaam the son of Beor that was sent for to curse Israel; he chased the reward and was slain.
precepts.point: With the princes of Midian, Balaam also the son of Beor, the soothsayer, did the children of Israel slay with the sword. This is the same Balaam from Numbers 22, the one whose ass saw the angel standing there to kill him when he could not see it himself. He was the one going after the lust of greed, and he ended up getting put to death.

note.label: Joshua 13: Much Land Yet to Be Possessed

precepts.why:
“Balaam also the son of Beor, the soothsayer, did the children of Israel slay with the sword among them that were slain by them.” This is the same Balaam from Numbers 22: “He sent messengers therefore unto Balaam the son of Beor to Pethor, which is by the river of the land of the children of his people, to call him”, sent for to curse Israel, the people come out from Egypt that “cover the face of the earth”.

He is the one whose ass saw the angel standing there to kill him when he could not see it himself. He was going after the lust of greed, chasing the reward, and it ended with him put to death with the sword alongside the princes of Midian, in the land that became the inheritance of the children of Reuben.
